data:
The wrapper records which job ran on which host. Start with Install, then read what you need.
You want to Read Install it Install Change a setting Configuration Know what is logged Event schema Understand what it does to a job How it works Run it on EC2 EC2 metadata Join it with CircleCI spans Join data with CircleCI OpenTelemetry Ship the data Alloy, Datadog Agent See a dashboard Example Grafana dashboard Judge the risk Security Fix a problem Troubleshooting, FAQ

All settings are environment variables of the runner process. They reach the wrapper because the runner passes its environment on. Five of them can also be KEY=value lines in the operator file (CCI_JOBLOG_CONF), marked file below. The file supplies defaults and the environment wins.
Variable Default Meaning CCI_JOBLOG_FILE /var/log/circleci-job-wrapper/jobs.jsonl JSONL output file. The directory is created if missing. Skipped silently if unwritable CCI_JOBLOG_STATE_DIR /run/circleci-job-wrapper Directory for the .json current-job files CCI_JOBLOG_STATE_ON_END remove remove deletes the state file at job end. idle rewrites it as {"state":"idle",...} CCI_JOBLOG_HOST_CACHE /run/circleci-job-wrapper/host.env Host identity cache (key=value) CCI_JOBLOG_CONF /etc/circleci-job-wrapper/wrapper.env Operator file. Parsed, never sourced CCI_JOBLOG_IMDS_URL http://169.254.169.254 Metadata endpoint. Override for tests CCI_RUNNER_CONFIG the parent’s --config, else /etc/circleci-runner/circleci-runner-config.yaml Runner config to read runner.name from CCI_RUNNER_NAME from the runner config Runner name. Wins over the config file (file) CCI_RESOURCE_CLASS empty Resource class (file) CCI_JOBLOG_EXTRA_FIELDS empty k=v,k=v, merged into every event as strings (file). Reserved names and keys containing token, secret, passw, credential, auth or apikey are skipped. 128 bytes per value CCI_JOBLOG_APP_URL https://app.circleci.com Base for workflow_url and pipeline_url. Set it for CircleCI Server CCI_JOBLOG_PROM_DIR empty (off) Write /.prom, a Prometheus textfile with the busy gauge (file) CCI_JOBLOG_PROM_JOB_ID empty 1 adds a job_id label to the busy gauge (file). One series per job: fine for small fleets, high cardinality otherwise CCI_JOBLOG_HTTP_URL empty (off) POST every event here, in the background, with --max-time 2 CCI_JOBLOG_HTTP_HEADER empty One extra header, for example Authorization: Bearer .... Passed to curl on stdin, so it is not visible in ps CCI_JOBLOG_FORWARD_SIGNALS 1 0 stops the wrapper forwarding TERM, INT and HUP to the agent CCI_JOBLOG_DISABLE empty Non-empty: exec the agent directly, with no telemetry. A kill switch CCI_JOBLOG_DEBUG empty Non-empty: diagnostics on stderr. Never secrets, never agent arguments
data.busy-gauge#Busy gauge:
With CCI_JOBLOG_PROM_DIR set, the wrapper also writes /.prom, a Prometheus textfile:
circleci_runner_busy{runner,resource_class,instance_id[,job_name,project,job_id]} 1|0 circleci_runner_job_start_time_seconds{...} # only while busy job_name and project are present while busy. CCI_JOBLOG_PROM_JOB_ID=1 adds job_id, one series per job, so use it on small fleets only. Read the file with Alloy’s prometheus.exporter.unix textfile collector or node_exporter’s --collector.textfile.directory.
data.logrotate#Logrotate:
logrotate/circleci-job-wrapper rotates daily, keeps 7 compressed files and uses copytruncate. The wrapper opens the file with O_APPEND for every event, so truncating in place is safe for any number of concurrent appenders. At worst, the lines written between logrotate’s copy and truncate are lost.
create would hand the new file to root and silently stop every runner account from logging, because the wrapper never fails a job over logging. For lossless rotation, use create 0664 instead.
data.resource-class#Resource class:
The runner config does not contain the resource class (the token maps to it), and the runner passes none in the job environment. Set it in the operator file:
# /etc/circleci-job-wrapper/wrapper.env (one file per host; not sourced) CCI_RESOURCE_CLASS=my-org/linux-large CCI_JOBLOG_EXTRA_FIELDS=team=infra,pool=bazel With several runners of different resource classes on one host, set CCI_RESOURCE_CLASS and CCI_RUNNER_NAME in each runner’s service environment instead. resolve_runner_and_class in the script has a marked HOOK for reading the class from a CIRCLE_* variable, should a future runner provide one.
data.runner-name#Runner name:
The wrapper uses the first of these:
CCI_RUNNER_NAME, or the operator file. The name: key directly under the top-level runner: key of the runner config. The config is CCI_RUNNER_CONFIG, else the --config argument of the parent runner process, else /etc/circleci-runner/circleci-runner-config.yaml. A tiny parser extracts only that one value. The api: and auth token lines are never stored, logged or used. With no name, the state file is called pid-.json.
data.state-file#State file:
/.json (name sanitised to [A-Za-z0-9._-]) is written atomically (temp file and mv) at job start and removed at job end. It has the same fields as job_start, plus "state":"running" and "updated_at".
A wrapper that is SIGKILLed cannot clean up, so treat a file whose wrapper_pid is no longer alive as stale. /run is tmpfs, so stale files vanish at reboot.

data:
The wrapper reads the instance identity from one request to the instance identity document (/latest/dynamic/instance-identity/document).
The instance metadata service (IMDS) must be enabled on the instance. On non-EC2 hosts, or with IMDS disabled, the EC2 fields are empty and nothing else changes. IMDSv2 works and is recommended (HttpTokens=required). The wrapper sends PUT /latest/api/token first and falls back to IMDSv1 only if that fails. Timeouts are 0.3 s to connect and 1 s in total per request, and proxies are bypassed. A hop limit of 1 is enough for jobs that run on the host, because the wrapper runs on the host itself. Use a hop limit of 2 only if the jobs themselves, for example containers they start, query IMDS. Instance metadata tags (InstanceMetadataTags=enabled) are optional and the wrapper does not read them. To put a tag such as Team on every event, read it once at boot (/latest/meta-data/tags/instance/) and write it to CCI_JOBLOG_EXTRA_FIELDS in the operator file.
data.cache#Cache:
The identity is cached in CCI_JOBLOG_HOST_CACHE (tmpfs by default) together with the kernel boot id, so a cache that survives in an image or a new boot is ignored.
The boot-time unit (circleci-job-wrapper --refresh-host-cache, 3 attempts) fills the cache, so no job ever queries IMDS. Without the unit, the first job on each boot fills it, while the job runs and never delaying its start. If the cache cannot be written, each job queries IMDS itself. A negative result (not on EC2) is cached for 300 s.

data:
The wrapper writes one JSON object per line (schema version 1), UTF-8. Each line is written with a single append and stays well under 4 KiB, so concurrent appends from many runner agents do not interleave.
All identifiers are strings, and a missing value is "", so every line has the same keys. job_end additionally has agent_exit_code, duration_ms, start_ms, end_ms and agent_status.
Field Source schema (number), event, ts job_start or job_end. ts is RFC 3339 UTC with milliseconds job_id CIRCLE_WORKFLOW_JOB_ID (fallback CIRCLE_JOB_ID). The join key: equals com.circleci.job.id on CircleCI spans job_name, job_number CIRCLE_JOB, CIRCLE_BUILD_NUM workflow_id, pipeline_id CIRCLE_WORKFLOW_ID, CIRCLE_PIPELINE_ID pipeline_number CIRCLE_PIPELINE_NUMBER. The runner does not provide it, so it is normally empty workflow_url, pipeline_url /workflow/ and /pipeline/. The base is CCI_JOBLOG_APP_URL project, org CIRCLE_PROJECT_REPONAME, CIRCLE_PROJECT_USERNAME org_id, project_id CIRCLE_ORGANIZATION_ID, CIRCLE_PROJECT_ID branch, sha, build_url, node_index CIRCLE_BRANCH, CIRCLE_SHA1, CIRCLE_BUILD_URL (the job link), CIRCLE_NODE_INDEX pr_number CIRCLE_PR_NUMBER. The runner does not provide it, so it is normally empty hostname The host’s name instance_id, instance_type, availability_zone, region, private_ip, ami_id EC2 instance identity document. Empty off EC2 runner_name, resource_class See Configuration wrapper_pid, agent_pid (numbers) The wrapper and the task agent process extra fields CCI_JOBLOG_EXTRA_FIELDS agent_exit_code, duration_ms, start_ms, end_ms (numbers), agent_status job_end only. start_ms and end_ms are epoch milliseconds agent_status is completed (the agent exited 0), agent_error, or cancelled (the wrapper received TERM, INT or HUP). It describes the agent process, not the job result. See How it works.
Only the variables listed here are ever read. The environment is never dumped and the agent’s command line is never logged. The CIRCLE_* names are read defensively, and any that the runner does not provide are empty.
data.example#Example: {"schema":1,"event":"job_start","ts":"2026-11-18T20:31:55.456Z","job_id":"5b1e0c1a-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","job_name":"build","job_number":"1234","workflow_id":"7f3d0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002","workflow_url":"https://app.circleci.com/workflow/7f3d0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002","pipeline_id":"a1b20000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","pipeline_url":"https://app.circleci.com/pipeline/a1b20000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","pipeline_number":"","project":"example-repo","org":"example-org","org_id":"c0de0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004","project_id":"d00d0000-0000-4000-8000-000000000005","branch":"main","sha":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567","build_url":"https://app.circleci.com/jobs/1234","node_index":"0","pr_number":"","hostname":"ip-10-0-1-23","instance_id":"i-0123456789abcdef0","instance_type":"c7g.xlarge","availability_zone":"us-east-1b","region":"us-east-1","private_ip":"10.0.1.23","ami_id":"ami-0abc1234def567890","runner_name":"runner-1","resource_class":"my-org/linux-large","wrapper_pid":1656458,"agent_pid":1656459,"team":"infra","pool":"bazel"} {"schema":1,"event":"job_end","ts":"2026-11-18T20:31:55.758Z","job_id":"5b1e0c1a-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","job_name":"build","...":"(same fields as job_start)","team":"infra","pool":"bazel","agent_exit_code":0,"duration_ms":302,"start_ms":1795033915456,"end_ms":1795033915758,"agent_status":"completed"} The "...": key in the second line only abbreviates this page. Real lines repeat all fields.

data:
examples/grafana/build_dashboard.py generates the dashboard JSON. Pass the datasource UIDs of your stack:
python3 examples/grafana/build_dashboard.py --prom --loki --tempo > dashboard.json # upload: POST /api/dashboards/db with {"dashboard": , "overwrite": true} For CircleCI Server, also pass --app-url so the links point at your installation. The dashboard needs the Alloy example data, and the CircleCI spans for the span panels.
data.panels#Panels: Fleet now. Busy and idle runners, hosts reporting, and a table of what each runner is doing (job, project, running for), from the busy gauge. Host health per instance: CPU, IO wait, memory, disk, network and load, with job starts as annotations. Jobs per host, from wrapper events. Job results per host, from the task agent’s “Reporting task end.” line, and job results from CircleCI spans. Failed jobs over time per host. A spike on one host is a wedged worker. Live step activity, from the task-agent journal. Recent jobs. Which host ran what, with a drill-down link per job. Job, workflow and pipeline IDs link to the CircleCI UI (build_url, workflow_url, pipeline_url). Per-job drill-down ($job_id). Where and when it ran, the result, steps slowest first (from spans), and host CPU and IO wait during the job window.

data.can-i-send-events-to-another-system#Can: Yes. Ship jobs.jsonl with any log shipper (Vector, Fluent Bit and others), or set CCI_JOBLOG_HTTP_URL to POST every event.
data.do-i-need-opentelemetry-or-grafana#Do I: No. The wrapper writes jobs.jsonl with nothing else. The OpenTelemetry export, a shipper and the dashboard are optional. See what you need.
data.does-it-change-my-jobs#Does it change my: No. The task agent runs as a normal child. Stdin is the same pipe, signals are forwarded, and the exit status is returned exactly. If logging fails, the job does not.
data.does-it-slow-jobs-down#Does it slow jobs: About 6 ms per job. The agent starts before any telemetry runs.
data.does-it-work-off-ec2#Does it work off EC: Yes. The EC2 fields are empty and everything else works.
data.does-it-work-with-circleci-server-contai: Not tested and not supported. The project targets machine runner 3.1.11 or later on Linux. CCI_JOBLOG_APP_URL exists for CircleCI Server links, but that setup was not tested.
data.is-the-agent_status-the-job-result#Is th: No. See How it works. Take the result from the CircleCI span or the task-agent journal.
data.where-do-i-ask-for-help#Where do I ask f: See Support on the home page.
data.why-a-wrapper-and-not-only-circlecis-ope: The spans carry the job result and timing, but no runner or host identity. The wrapper adds the host. If CircleCI later adds that to the built-in runner telemetry, you may not need this project.
data.why-is-the-task-agent-journal-pipeline-e: It reads the task agent’s internal log lines, and that format may change between runner versions.

data.agent_status-is-not-the-job-result#agent:
The task agent exits 0 even when the job fails or is cancelled from the UI. So completed only means the agent process exited 0. Take the job result from the CircleCI span (com.circleci.job.status) or, on the host, from the task agent’s own “Reporting task end.” log line (see Ship with Grafana Alloy).
cancelled only means the wrapper received TERM, INT or HUP, for example because the runner is stopping a task.
data.environment-the-runner-provides#Environm:
Verified on machine runner 3.1.14, these built-in variables reach the command_prefix process (names only):
CIRCLE_BRANCH CIRCLE_BUILD_NUM CIRCLE_BUILD_URL CIRCLE_JOB CIRCLE_NODE_INDEX CIRCLE_NODE_TOTAL CIRCLE_ORGANIZATION_ID CIRCLE_PIPELINE_ID CIRCLE_PROJECT_ID CIRCLE_PROJECT_REPONAME CIRCLE_PROJECT_USERNAME CIRCLE_REPOSITORY_URL CIRCLE_SHA1 CIRCLE_USERNAME CIRCLE_WORKFLOW_ID CIRCLE_WORKFLOW_JOB_ID CIRCLE_WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE_ID
There is no resource class, pipeline number or PR number, so those event fields stay empty unless you supply them. For the resource class, see Configuration.
data.how-command_prefix-invokes-the-wrapper#H:
With this runner config:
runner: command_prefix: ["/usr/local/bin/circleci-job-wrapper"] the runner executes
/usr/local/bin/circleci-job-wrapper with the job’s built-in environment (CIRCLE_*) added and the task token on stdin. The wrapper:
Starts the task agent as a child with <&0, so stdin is the very same pipe. While the job already runs, resolves the host identity and writes job_start and the state file. The cost to job start-up is one fork. Waits for the child. If the wrapper itself gets SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP, it forwards the signal to the child. Writes job_end, removes the state file, and exits with the child’s exit code (128+n for a signalled child). Every helper command the wrapper runs has
data.multiple-runners-on-one-host#Multiple ru: Several runner agents share one wrapper, one log file and one cache. Each event carries its runner_name, and each runner has its own state file. See Install.
data.overhead#Overhead: About 6 ms per job. The agent is spawned before any telemetry runs. Logging is best effort: every logging failure is swallowed, and the wrapper is silent unless CCI_JOBLOG_DEBUG is set. It needs bash 4 or later and POSIX utilities, with no jq, no daemon and no Python.
data.signals#Signals:
When the runner stops a task, it sends SIGTERM to the command_prefix process only, not the process group. It sends SIGKILL to the whole process group after 10 s, or immediately with enable_unsafe_retries. So:
Signal forwarding (on by default) is required. Otherwise the agent never sees the SIGTERM. If the agent has not exited within 10 s, the wrapper is killed too and job_end is lost. Consumers must tolerate a job_start without a job_end. A cancel from the CircleCI UI is handled by the agent itself (exit 0, no signal), so it shows as completed.
data.stdin#stdin: The task token stays on the agent’s stdin. The wrapper never reads or redirects it.

data:
Install the wrapper on every host that runs a machine runner. You need machine runner 3.1.11 or later on Linux, with bash 4 or later and the POSIX utilities date, curl, mkdir, mv and rm.
Install the wrapper.
sudo install -m 0755 bin/circleci-job-wrapper /usr/local/bin/circleci-job-wrapper Create the directories. The runner user must be able to write both.
sudo install -d -m 0775 -o root -g circleci /var/log/circleci-job-wrapper sudo install -d -m 1777 /run/circleci-job-wrapper # or let systemd do it, see step 3 Install the boot-time host cache (recommended).
sudo install -m 0644 systemd/circleci-job-wrapper-hostcache.service /etc/systemd/system/ sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl enable --now circleci-job-wrapper-hostcache.service Install log rotation (recommended).
sudo install -m 0644 logrotate/circleci-job-wrapper /etc/logrotate.d/circleci-job-wrapper Set the resource class (recommended). The file is parsed, never sourced.
sudo install -d /etc/circleci-job-wrapper echo 'CCI_RESOURCE_CLASS=my-org/linux-large' | sudo tee /etc/circleci-job-wrapper/wrapper.env Add the prefix to the runner config (/etc/circleci-runner/circleci-runner-config.yaml), then restart the runner.
runner: command_prefix: ["/usr/local/bin/circleci-job-wrapper"] Run a job and check the log.
tail -n2 /var/log/circleci-job-wrapper/jobs.jsonl Replace circleci with the account and group your runner service runs as.
data.run-the-tests#Run the tests: make check runs shellcheck and the bats tests. It needs bats, jq, python3 and curl. strace and iconv are used when present.
data.several-runner-agents-on-one-host#Severa: Agents on one host share the wrapper, the log file and the cache. This was tested with two systemd units (circleci-runner and circleci-runner-b), each with its own -c config file and runner.name. The wrapper reads the name from the parent’s -c or --config argument, so nothing more is needed, and events from both interleave safely. Set CCI_RUNNER_NAME in a unit’s environment only to override the name.
data.what-the-host-cache-unit-does#What the h:
The unit runs circleci-job-wrapper --refresh-host-cache once per boot. It creates two directories:
/run/circleci-job-wrapper, sticky with mode 1777, so runner accounts can write state files but cannot replace the root-owned host.env. /var/log/circleci-job-wrapper, mode 0775. Add a Group= in a drop-in to match the runner group.

data:
CircleCI’s own OpenTelemetry job, step and task spans carry com.circleci.resource.class and com.circleci.job.status, but no runner or host identity. They are sent when each job finishes. The wrapper and the host agents add the where and the live view. Everything joins on two keys: job_id and instance_id.
Source Carries Join key Wrapper events (jobs.jsonl) job_id, workflow_id, instance_id, runner_name, resource_class, start and end job_id = CIRCLE_WORKFLOW_JOB_ID CircleCI spans (OTLP exporter) Job result (com.circleci.job.status), resource class, step spans and durations com.circleci.job.id = job_id Host metrics (Alloy unix exporter, textfile busy gauge) CPU, memory, disk, network, busy or idle per runner instance_id label Task-agent journal (optional, experimental) Step start and end, the job result as the host sees it, in near real time job-id = job_id, plus instance_id job_id ----------+--> wrapper events ---+ +--> CircleCI spans ---+--> one job: where, when, result, steps +--> task-agent log ---+ instance_id -----+--> host metrics -----+--> what the host was doing meanwhile To receive the spans, set up the OpenTelemetry export of your CircleCI organization with CircleCI’s exporter API (POST /api/v2/otel/exporters). See Ship with Grafana Alloy for a worked example, and CircleCI’s documentation for the current API.
To report a vulnerability, read SECURITY.md.
data.what-the-wrapper-reads-and-writes#What t: Allow-list only. The wrapper reads fixed CIRCLE_* names, the host identity and the operator settings. Tokens (CIRCLE_TOKEN and similar), the environment and the agent’s arguments are never read into a log call. The runner config is read only to find runner.name. The auth token line is not kept, logged or used. /proc//cmdline is read only to find the --config path. Operator files and the cache are parsed as key=value, never sourced. The task token stays on the agent’s stdin. The wrapper never reads or redirects it, and all helper commands run with
data.what-you-should-decide#What you should d: The log is world-readable by default (0644, as created by the first writer) and contains project, branch and user-controlled strings. Restrict the directory if that matters. /run/circleci-job-wrapper is sticky and mode 1777, like /tmp, so runner users cannot delete each other’s state files or replace the root-owned host.env. Tighten it (for example 0775 with a Group=) if all runners share one account. Signal forwarding is what lets the agent shut down cleanly, because the runner sends SIGTERM to the wrapper only. Set CCI_JOBLOG_FORWARD_SIGNALS=0 only if you must. Extra fields skip keys that look like secrets, but only the operator should write the operator file.

data:
examples/alloy/config.alloy ships the wrapper events, the optional task-agent journal lines and host metrics to any OTLP/HTTP endpoint. It is tested with Grafana Cloud. Its blocks:
File tail to Loki over OTLP. local.file_match and loki.source.file tail jobs.jsonl. loki.process promotes event, resource_class, runner and instance_id to labels. Job and workflow IDs stay in the JSON body, queried with | json. otelcol.receiver.loki and otelcol.processor.transform turn the stream into OTLP logs named circleci-job-wrapper. Journal pipeline (optional, experimental). loki.source.journal reads the runner units’ journal. The task agent writes JSON lines there. loki.process keeps only Runner started execution, step start, step end and Reporting task end. (each has a job-id) and labels them event=task_start|step_start|step_end|task_end, log_type=task_agent and instance_id. This gives near-real-time step progress and the job result per host. It is an internal format and may change between runner versions. Edit matches to list your runner units. Host metrics. prometheus.exporter.unix with its textfile collector pointed at CCI_JOBLOG_PROM_DIR, scraped every 15 s into otelcol.receiver.prometheus. EC2 identity. otelcol.processor.resourcedetection with the ec2 and system detectors sets host.id (the instance ID) on logs and metrics. instance_id on metrics. otelcol.processor.transform "metrics" copies host.id into an instance_id datapoint attribute, so metrics join with the wrapper’s instance_id. Export. otelcol.exporter.otlphttp with otelcol.auth.basic.
data.circleci-spans-to-grafana#CircleCI spans:
Send CircleCI’s OpenTelemetry spans to the same stack with CircleCI’s exporter API (POST /api/v2/otel/exporters):
Endpoint: the gateway URL above with /v1/traces appended. Protocol: http. Header: Authorization: Basic . The spans then land in Tempo, with com.circleci.job.id matching the wrapper’s job_id.
data.environment#Environment:
For example in /etc/default/alloy:
Variable Meaning OTLP_ENDPOINT OTLP/HTTP base URL. For Grafana Cloud, the stack’s region gateway, https://otlp-gateway-.grafana.net/otlp OTLP_USERNAME Grafana Cloud instance (stack) ID OTLP_PASSWORD Access token with write scope. Never commit it EC2_INSTANCE_ID This host’s instance ID, used for the journal lines. Write it at install time from IMDSv2 (/latest/meta-data/instance-id)
data.permissions#Permissions: The alloy user needs read access to jobs.jsonl: add it to the runner’s group. The journal pipeline also needs membership of systemd-journal. The textfile directory must be readable by alloy too.

data:
This is documented but not tested in this repository. See Datadog’s custom log collection and Prometheus host collection.
Enable logs in datadog.yaml: logs_enabled: true.
Create /etc/datadog-agent/conf.d/circleci_job_wrapper.d/conf.yaml:
logs: - type: file path: /var/log/circleci-job-wrapper/jobs.jsonl service: circleci-job-wrapper source: circleci Datadog parses the JSON into attributes. Make @job_id, @instance_id and @runner_name facets.
Add the dd-agent user to the runner’s group so it can read the file.
Optional: add a second type: journald source for the runner units, with include_units, to get the task agent’s step and result lines. The same caveat applies: the format is internal.
Host metrics come from the Agent’s built-in system checks. On EC2, the host is identified by its instance ID.
For the busy gauge, point the Agent’s OpenMetrics check at node_exporter’s textfile collector, or build Datadog log-based metrics from job_start and job_end.
CircleCI spans reach Datadog through its OTLP intake (the Agent’s or a Collector’s OTLP receiver, or Datadog’s OTLP endpoint), using the same CircleCI exporter API as in Ship with Grafana Alloy.

The wrapper never fails a job over logging, so a problem usually shows up as missing data, not as an error. Turn on diagnostics first: set CCI_JOBLOG_DEBUG=1 in the runner service environment, restart the runner, and read the runner’s journal.
data.a-job_start-has-no-job_end#A job_start h: This is expected when the runner kills the wrapper with SIGKILL. See How it works. Treat a state file whose wrapper_pid is gone as stale.
data.alloy-cannot-read-the-log-or-the-journal: Add the alloy user to the runner’s group so it can read jobs.jsonl, and restart Alloy. For the journal pipeline, add alloy to the systemd-journal group. Make the CCI_JOBLOG_PROM_DIR directory readable by alloy. Check that matches in config.alloy lists your runner units. Then read the Alloy log for permission denied or no such file.
data.ec2-fields-are-empty#EC2 fields are empt: Check that IMDS is enabled on the instance, and that you are on EC2. See EC2 metadata. Check the cache: cat /run/circleci-job-wrapper/host.env (it contains the instance identity, not secrets). If the unit failed, run systemctl status circleci-job-wrapper-hostcache.service. A negative result is cached for 300 s. After you fix IMDS, run sudo /usr/local/bin/circleci-job-wrapper --refresh-host-cache.
data.jobsjsonl-is-missing-or-empty#jobs.jsonl: Check that the runner uses the wrapper: command_prefix in the runner config must be ["/usr/local/bin/circleci-job-wrapper"], and the runner must have been restarted after the change. Check that the file is executable: ls -l /usr/local/bin/circleci-job-wrapper. Check that CCI_JOBLOG_DISABLE is not set in the runner’s environment. Check the permissions below.
data.permission-denied-on-the-log-directory#P:
The wrapper appends as the runner user, and skips logging silently if it cannot write. Check that /var/log/circleci-job-wrapper is writable by that user:
sudo -u circleci test -w /var/log/circleci-job-wrapper && echo writable Replace circleci with your runner user. Fix it with a group-writable directory (mode 0775, owned by the runner group), or a Group= drop-in for the host cache unit. If logrotate recreated the file as root, switch to copytruncate as in the shipped config.
data.resource_class-is-empty#resource_class i: The runner does not tell the wrapper its resource class. Set CCI_RESOURCE_CLASS in the operator file. See Configuration.
data.runner_name-is-empty-or-the-state-file-i: The wrapper could not find runner.name. Set CCI_RUNNER_NAME in the runner’s environment or the operator file, or check that the runner config has a name: key directly under runner:. See Configuration.
